text:
Philadelphia arrives on the second night of a back-to-back, still stinging from last night's 4-3 overtime loss to CBJ, where Kent Johnson ended it. The Flyers are 3-1-1 in their last five but are missing Travis Konecny, Owen Tippett and Rasmus Ristolainen. Trevor Zegras has stepped in beside Christian Dvorak and Matvei Michkov, and Porter Martone has moved onto the first power-play unit. Washington has had three days off since coming back from two goals down to beat BUF 4-3 in overtime, with Alex Tuch scoring the winner.

Our numbers favor the Capitals (3.41 expected goals to 2.73). At five on five, WSH has taken 52% of the expected goals, a measure of chance quality, while PHI is at 40%. PHI's power play is the better one by that measure, but WSH takes 4.4 penalties a game. Projected goalies Joseph Woll (+4.2 goals saved above expected) and Logan Thompson (+4.5) are close this season. Thompson was +28.16 last year to Woll's -7.44.

Michkov has 9 points in his last ten games, and The New York Times wrote that he is "lighting up the scoresheet" after logging off Instagram. We have him at 30% to score and Zegras at 29% on a 5-game point streak. For Washington, Tuch leads at 39% to score. Our under-the-radar picks are Ryan Leonard, a third-liner whose shots have been dangerous lately (25% to score), and Martone, 45% for a point as his minutes grow.
